items.title: Lemaitre before Hubble
items.claim: Hubble's 1929 paper reported a relationship between galaxy distance and redshift, indicating expansion. Who derived the relationship two years earlier?
items.reveal:
Lemaitre's 1927 paper in Annales de la Societe Scientifique de Bruxelles included an estimate of the expansion rate.

The IAU resolved in 2018 to refer to the law as the Hubble-Lemaitre Law.
items.why: Language and journal of publication shape who gets credited for foundational results.

items.title: Why we infer dark matter
items.claim: Vera Rubin and Kent Ford in the 1970s measured spiral galaxy rotation curves. What did they find?

options.text: Rotation slowed at the edges as Keplerian dynamics would predict
Rotation stayed roughly flat at large radii, implying more mass than visible matter accounted for

items.reveal_title: Flat rotation curves implied invisible mass
items.reveal:
Rubin and Ford's 1970s observations confirmed earlier hints (Zwicky 1933 on cluster dynamics).

Current cosmological models attribute roughly 27% of the universe's mass-energy budget to dark matter, 68% to dark energy and around 5% to baryonic matter.
items.why: Most of what controls galactic dynamics is something we cannot see directly.

items.title: Why Pluto was reclassified
items.claim: The IAU's 2006 definition of 'planet' has three conditions: it orbits the Sun, has enough mass for hydrostatic equilibrium, and what?
items.reveal_title: 'Cleared the neighbourhood' is the criterion Pluto fails
items.reveal:
Pluto orbits within the Kuiper Belt with comparable bodies (notably Eris). The IAU created the 'dwarf planet' category.

Ceres in the asteroid belt is also a dwarf planet under the definition.
items.why: Scientific categories sometimes change to track the evidence rather than vice versa.
